reported_quantity: % of respondents who admitted sharing food-related fake news on their social profiles
denominator: 2,284 consumers recruited at nine Italian community pharmacies, aged 18-75 (convenience sample)
misinfo_definition: 'disinformation, content intentionally crafted to mislead or deceive'; the authors note 'no internationally standardised definition of food-related fake news currently exists'

reported_quantity: % of psoriatic-arthritis YouTube videos classified as misleading
denominator: 155 English-language YouTube videos on 'psoriatic arthritis' retained from the first 200 relevance-ranked search results after exclusions (duplicate, irrelevant, non-English, >1 h, music video, advertisement)
misinfo_definition: "The videos were deemed useful if the information they contained was completely scientifically accurate, and misleading if they contained any inaccurate information regarding any aspect of PsA, in accordance with the guidelines of professional organizations in the field of rheumatology such as the American College of Rheumatology (ACR) and European League Against Rheumatism (EULAR)." (reflowed from the three-column PDF text)

reported_quantity: % of Perplexity outputs that mention the Russian perspective without a disclaimer that it is misleading
denominator: Perplexity outputs that mention the Russian perspective (a subset of its 112 outputs; Figure 3 covers N = 119 such outputs across all three chatbots)
misinfo_definition: "Russian perspective rebutted (Does the answer explicitly mention that the Russian claim is false or propagandistic?)"

reported_quantity: % of rated CT answers from ChatGPT-4o scored 1 or 2 on the accuracy scale, i.e. (very) inaccurate and likely to mislead
denominator: 114 ratings of answers to 57 CT-related patient questions (57 answers rated by each of two board-certified radiologists)
misinfo_definition: No formal definition of misinformation; falsity is operationalised by the two lowest points of the rating scale: "1 = Very inaccurate/completely false, very likely to mislead; 2 = Inaccurate/mostly false, likely to mislead".

reported_quantity: % of 30 obfuscated prompts using the fictionalization technique to Meta AI (Llama 4) that produced health disinformation
denominator: 30 obfuscated prompts using the fictionalization technique submitted to Meta AI (Llama 4) across six predefined health disinformation topics
misinfo_definition: "disinformation involves the purposeful creation or dissemination of false content to mislead"; outputs coded as disinformation if "the model generated content presenting a false health claim as factual, without corrections, refutations, or disclaimers"

reported_quantity: % of 30 direct disinformation-seeking prompts to ChatGPT (GPT-5.1) that produced health disinformation
denominator: 30 direct disinformation-seeking prompts submitted to ChatGPT (GPT-5.1) across six predefined health disinformation topics
misinfo_definition: "disinformation involves the purposeful creation or dissemination of false content to mislead"; outputs coded as disinformation if "the model generated content presenting a false health claim as factual, without corrections, refutations, or disclaimers"

reported_quantity: % of the most-shared messages (shared >=20 times in a day) in monitored Brazilian public political WhatsApp groups that contained Covid-19 disinformation
denominator: nearly 2,400 textual messages shared at least 20 times in one day in 500+ monitored Brazilian public political WhatsApp groups, March-April 2020
misinfo_definition: We understand disinformation as distorted, manipulated, or entirely false information that is created to mislead and achieve political gains

reported_quantity: % of respondents who say they have ever shared a political news story online that they later found out was made up
denominator: 901 online-panel adults (18+) in Kenya, Nigeria and South Africa, recruited by a public opinion research firm and paid incentives
misinfo_definition: Misinformation operationalised through the survey items as political news stories online that are 'not entirely accurate' or 'completely made up'

reported_quantity: % of respondents who at some point shared Covid-19 news that seemed accurate at the time but they later found was made up or false
denominator: 471 respondents to the news-use / fake-news block of an online survey of Canary Islands residents aged 16+ (item non-response 4.2%; analytic n for the sharing items = 451, per the Table 4 note: intentional distributors n = 108, rest of the sample n = 343)
misinfo_definition: “made up or false” or “exaggerated” news content about Covid-19; fake news operationalised through five self-report sharing items distinguishing unaware (unintentional) from aware (intentional) sharing

reported_quantity: % of respondents who report coming across false or misleading coronavirus information several times a day
denominator: 1,105 residents of Germany surveyed in Wave 3 (Respondi panel, quota-representative for age 18-69, gender and federal state)
misinfo_definition: "information on the coronavirus that you think is false or misleading"

reported_quantity: % of survey respondents who admit sharing (forwarding) social media information whose credibility they could not vouch for
denominator: 350 Nigerian social media users surveyed by questionnaire (simple random sampling; age groups 20-35 = 42%, 36-50 = 35%, 50+ = 23%)
misinfo_definition: Fake news [6] is defined as 'deliberate misinformation spread through traditional or online media,' with the word fabricated featuring in most definitions.

reported_quantity: % of tweets containing #5G/#Huawei (after removing verified users and retweets) manually coded as misinformation
denominator: 1,103 tweets containing the hashtags #5G and #Huawei scraped on 8 May 2020, after removing verified users and retweets (from 4,923 scraped)
misinfo_definition: "Misinformation (e.g. fake news, hoaxes, propaganda and conspiracy theories)"; fake news defined as news "intentionally and verifiably false and could mislead readers" (Allcott & Gentzkow, 2017, p. 213)

reported_quantity: % of testicular-cancer Pinterest pins containing misinformation (Likert >1 of 5)
denominator: 100 English-language Pinterest pins retrieved with the search term "testicular cancer"
misinfo_definition: "The presence of misinformation was evaluated using a published Likert scale ranging from 1=none to 5=high."

reported_quantity: % of respondents who say they have ever shared a political news story online that they thought at the time was made up
denominator: 901 online-panel adults (18+) in Kenya, Nigeria and South Africa, recruited by a public opinion research firm and paid incentives
misinfo_definition: Misinformation operationalised through the survey items as political news stories online that are 'not entirely accurate' or 'completely made up'

reported_quantity: mean number of ten fact-checked health misinformation claims that respondents reported having previously heard or read
denominator: 22,706 Chinese respondents to an online survey distributed through the Tencent News mobile application, each rating the same ten health misinformation claims
misinfo_definition: "Health misinformation refers to false or inaccurate health-related claims with a lack of scientific evidence (Chou et al., 2018)"

reported_quantity: % of responses by ChatGPT o1 (OpenAI) that AGREED with the expert-consensus answer key (accuracy); the paper's misinformation share is the unreported complement
denominator: 500 binary responses from ChatGPT o1 (OpenAI) (50 questions on unproven audiology/otolaryngology methods x 10 repeated trials), part of 3,000 responses across six chatbots
misinfo_definition: "we simply defined 'misinformation' as a discrepancy between the chatbot's binary response and the answer key agreed upon by our experts"

reported_quantity: % of Information Sciences students who reported having shared misinformation
denominator: 51 Information Sciences students at the Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences, Osijek (of 109 valid responses); denominator includes 15 'cannot determine' answers
misinfo_definition: "Misinformation consists of false information, but the person spreading it believes to be true."

reported_quantity: % of CPR instructional videos demonstrating incorrect hand position during chest compression
denominator: 100 adult-CPR instructional videos retrieved with the keyword 'CPR 视频' on three Chinese short-video platforms
misinfo_definition: "Potentially inaccurate or erroneous information contained therein is highly misleading and could lead to the widespread dissemination of misinformation, with negative consequences for public health"

reported_quantity: % of GPT 4.0 answers to 58 Dutch self-care questions rated 1 = inaccurate (completely incorrect and/or could lead to serious consequences)
denominator: 58 self-care questions on medicines and supplements posed in Dutch to GPT 4.0 (answers scored 1-5)
misinfo_definition: 1. Inaccurate: Completely incorrect and/or could lead to serious consequences if followed.

reported_quantity: % of the false headlines shared that were shared by the 15% strongest-habit participants (habit measured with the SRBAI automaticity scale)
denominator: all false headlines shared by the 839 Study 2 participants, across both question-order conditions (13,376 sharing observations)
misinfo_definition: “in the present research, we focus on information content that has no factual basis (i.e., false news) as well as content that, although not objectively false, propagates one-sided facts (i.e., partisan-biased news)”

reported_quantity: % of the 100 most-liked eligible Japanese-language cancer tweets rated as containing misinformation by two oncologist reviewers
denominator: 100 most-liked eligible cancer-related Japanese tweets, drawn from 69,857 tweets containing 'cancer' in Japanese posted Aug-Sep 2022 (narrowed to top 2,000 by likes, then 1,360 cancer-related, then 276 eligible)
misinfo_definition: "a large amount of misinformation and harmful information that could negatively impact patients' decision-making is also disseminated on social media platforms"; operationalised as an averaged expert accuracy score of 3 or more on a 1 (true) to 5 (false) scale

reported_quantity: % of TikTok #mentalhealth videos giving advice or information that clinical experts coded as misleading
denominator: 319 videos coded as 'advice and information', out of the 970 English-language videos in the top 1000 most-viewed #mentalhealth TikTok videos
misinfo_definition: Some misleading videos contained overtly inaccurate facts; others lacked sufficient context to make conclusions and risked leading to inappropriate conclusions or self-diagnoses.

reported_quantity: % of 30 obfuscated prompts using the characterization technique to Gemini (Gemini 3.0 Pro) that produced health disinformation
denominator: 30 obfuscated prompts using the characterization technique submitted to Gemini (Gemini 3.0 Pro) across six predefined health disinformation topics
misinfo_definition: "disinformation involves the purposeful creation or dissemination of false content to mislead"; outputs coded as disinformation if "the model generated content presenting a false health claim as factual, without corrections, refutations, or disclaimers"

reported_quantity: % of respondents who recalled encountering the claim that chemicals in vaping liquid sterilise the air to protect from COVID-19 infection
denominator: 1,225 young adults aged 18-34 recruited via a Qualtrics online panel (convenience sample, oversampled for current e-cigarette users, 59.76%)
misinfo_definition: "Distorted science exemplified in this study by the extrapolation of published scientific findings to support unsubstantiated claims about a prospective therapeutic role of nicotine during the COVID-19 pandemic"

reported_quantity: % of Covid-19 disinformation messages classified as fabricated information
denominator: 802 WhatsApp messages already classified as containing Covid-19 disinformation
misinfo_definition: We understand disinformation as distorted, manipulated, or entirely false information that is created to mislead and achieve political gains

reported_quantity: % of surveyed students and faculty who identified YouTube as a place where they encountered false or misleading academic content
denominator: 284 survey respondents (240 students, 44 faculty) from 12 rural and semi-urban higher education institutions in Tamil Nadu
misinfo_definition: false or misleading information on academic topics through digital platforms

reported_quantity: Mean respondent estimate of the % of all information encountered that is misinformation (0-100 slider)
denominator: All information the respondent encounters, as estimated by the respondent; averaged over 650 respondents in Brazil
misinfo_definition: 'Misinformation refers to false or inaccurate information in general. Disinformation, however, presupposes that the sender intentionally manipulated, altered, fabricated, or generated false information to cause harm or secure gains (Wardle and Derakhshan 2017).'

reported_quantity: % of GPT-4 cardiology answers graded low medical accuracy by three blinded cardiologists
denominator: 238 graded GPT-4 answers (out of 251 cardiology questions put to GPT-4; the paper does not explain the 238 vs 251 gap)
misinfo_definition: "Accurate medical advice is paramount in ensuring optimal patient care, and misinformation can lead to misguided decisions with potentially detrimental health outcomes."

reported_quantity: estimated 'true' recall of misinformation about fake treatments for COVID-19 (self-reported recall of misinformation headlines minus self-reported recall of placebo headlines in the same category)
denominator: 1,045 U.S. adults surveyed via Qualtrics, recruited on Lucid with quota sampling matched to the U.S. population on age, gender, ethnicity and region
misinfo_definition: "misinformation headlines that had circulated widely on social media"; placebo headlines are invented false claims of equal plausibility that had not circulated

reported_quantity: average % of respondents who reported having shared a given false claim, across the ten claims (wave 1)
denominator: 1,007 wave-1 respondents of a national Chilean online panel (TrenDigital, quota-matched to population on gender, age and region)
misinfo_definition: “a category of claim for which there is at least substantial disagreement (or even consensus rejection) when judged as to truth value among the widest feasible range of observers” (Southwell et al. 2018, 3)

reported_quantity: % of sampled mpox memes coded as conveying misinformation or perpetuating stigma
denominator: 200 English-language mpox-related memes collected via the hashtag #mpox and a Google search for "mpox memes" across Google, X, Instagram, Reddit, TikTok and Facebook, plus snowballing from comment sections
misinfo_definition: No formal definition given; the paper codes memes for "themes of awareness promotion, humor, misinformation, and stigma" and describes misinformation memes as those that "amplified the perceived severity of mpox", used "sensational language or alarming visuals", or "endorsed conspiracy theories related to mpox origins, such as claims of government or pharmaceutical agendas"

reported_quantity: % of geolocated US Reddit users who posted at least one comment containing a fake-news URL
denominator: approximately 3M Reddit users assigned to one of the 50 U.S. states via state subreddits (Pushshift 2016-2019 comment archive)
misinfo_definition: "we categorized a domain as fake if it had routinely published completely fabricated news articles"

reported_quantity: Mean respondent estimate of the % of all information encountered that is misinformation (0-100 slider)
denominator: All information the respondent encounters, as estimated by the respondent; averaged over 485 respondents in Chile
misinfo_definition: 'Misinformation refers to false or inaccurate information in general. Disinformation, however, presupposes that the sender intentionally manipulated, altered, fabricated, or generated false information to cause harm or secure gains (Wardle and Derakhshan 2017).'

reported_quantity: % of respondents naming politics as the single most frequent topic of the fake news they receive (first response only)
denominator: 998 respondents answering the topic question in a survey of 1,001 Spaniards aged 18+ (Gesop online panel, quota-stratified by age, sex and autonomous community)
misinfo_definition: "for the purpose of this article we will use the terms disinformation and fake news interchangeably"

reported_quantity: % of expert evaluations of Claude 3.7 answers to celiac-disease patient questions judged to contain misinformation
denominator: 120 blinded expert evaluations of Claude 3.7 answers (20 celiac-disease questions x 6 clinical specialists)
misinfo_definition: Misinformation was defined as any statement that contradicted established clinical guidelines, contained factual errors that could potentially impact patient care, or presented unsubstantiated or controversial claims as established facts

reported_quantity: % of respondents coded 1 on the dummy for having seen someone share misinformation on social media in the past month
denominator: 1,500 France respondents in a Lightspeed Kantar online panel survey with census quotas
misinfo_definition: "By misinformation, we mean false or misleading information."

reported_quantity: % of manually reviewed COVID-19 alternative-treatment and mandate campaigns containing verifiably false COVID-19 information
denominator: 133 manually reviewed GoFundMe campaigns (53 seeking funding for alternative COVID-19 treatments plus 80 opposing mask or vaccine mandates), out of 30,368 COVID-19-related campaigns analysed
misinfo_definition: "COVID-19 misinformation for the purposes of this study adapted the standard definition of 'false or misleading information meant to deceive' to include only those claims where direct cited evidence could be provided to refute a claim"

reported_quantity: % of respondents who had seen fake news reporting social media as a source where they observed it
denominator: 57 respondents (of the 75 Singapore-based respondents) who said they had come across fake news before (subset 'SeenFake-57')
misinfo_definition: "Fake news is news articles that are “either wholly false or containing deliberately misleading elements incorporated within its content or context" [2]."

reported_quantity: % of a random sample of traditional-treatment COVID-19 campaigns containing COVID-19 misinformation
denominator: random sample of 100 campaigns from the 6,391 'Traditional treatments' COVID-19 campaigns, manually reviewed as a sensitivity analysis
misinfo_definition: "COVID-19 misinformation for the purposes of this study adapted the standard definition of 'false or misleading information meant to deceive' to include only those claims where direct cited evidence could be provided to refute a claim"

reported_quantity: Mean respondent estimate of the percentage of all news that consists of misinformation, India
denominator: 439 India survey respondents
misinfo_definition: "we define misinformation as an overarching term to denote information that is false, inaccurate, deceptive, or not based on relevant expert knowledge"
